findings.description: Critical: The coordinator plan replaces api_key_identities but does not explicitly replace the separate api_keys allowlist. Current ApiConfig.from_env retains COORDINATION_API_KEYS and derives an allowlist only once, while _principal_for_api_key accepts any key in that list even when no identity row exists. A rotated key could therefore stay authorized after snapshot replacement or an old static key could authenticate as an unbound principal after configured OpenBao failure.
findings.resolution: Specify and test one atomic authentication state containing both accepted keys and their identities. In configured OpenBao mode, reject keys absent from the current valid snapshot regardless of COORDINATION_API_KEYS; apply the 120-second age gate to every key path and explicitly define any non-agent service-key exception.

findings.description: Critical: wp-dispatch may edit only api_key_resolver.py and its tests, but review_dispatcher.py still passes openbao_role_id plus api_key_env to resolve() and constructs those values from agent roster fields. The new canonical-principal/requested-vendor lookup cannot be called from this site within the package write scope; leaving it unchanged preserves the legacy role override and environment fallback interface.
findings.resolution: Assign review_dispatcher.py and focused tests to wp-dispatch, update adapter construction and both SDK/OpenAI call sites to pass canonical principal and vendor, and add an end-to-end dispatch assertion that an undeclared vendor fails before any Bao read.

findings.description: Critical: The change removes BAO_SECRET_ID and shared-path agent access, but profile_loader.py still authenticates with OpenBaoConfig.create_client() using BAO_SECRET_ID and reads BAO_SECRET_PATH for coordinator profile secrets. No work package can edit profile_loader.py. The plan promises coordinator-internal and dynamic-database secret behavior remains unchanged without defining how this live consumer will authenticate after the configuration change.
findings.resolution: Define the retained coordinator-internal credential contract separately from agent identity bootstrap, then allocate profile_loader.py and its tests to an owning package. Verify profile interpolation and dynamic database credentials with Bao configured through migration and rollback.

findings.description: Critical: The seeder currently receives one flat .secrets.yaml document, while the plan requires per-agent API-key documents and per-vendor documents. Design D3 acknowledges ambiguous mappings but neither the contracts nor tasks define the explicit operator input format or how a flat source key maps to each destination. Without this, the seeder cannot populate all required paths deterministically or preflight complete migration before mutation.
findings.resolution: Add a versioned migration input schema or concrete CLI mapping format keyed by canonical agent and vendor, define validation for missing/duplicate destinations and unused source fields, and assign a RED test plus seeder implementation task before cutover.

findings.description: Critical: review_dispatcher.py creates a fresh ApiKeyResolver for each dispatch invocation, but the planned bootstrap bundle contains a single-use wrapped SecretID and no persisted client token. After the first process unwraps and logs in, a later dispatch process cannot authenticate from the same bundle. The design says rebootstrap is an operator action after token expiry, yet does not provide a protected token cache or a fresh-bundle delivery path for normal repeated dispatches.
findings.resolution: Define the dispatch credential session lifecycle before implementation: either a protected renewable token broker/cache shared across invocations or an authorized fresh wrapped SecretID delivery flow for each process. Specify storage permissions, concurrency, renewal/max-TTL behavior, and tests for two sequential dispatch processes and simultaneous dispatches.

findings.description: Nit: OpenBaoConfig and the current seeder support BAO_MOUNT_PATH, including non-default mounts, but principal-topology.schema.json fixes mount to 'secret' and every policy path in contracts/README.md starts with secret/data. The configuration spec calls secret the default, leaving it unclear whether non-default mounts remain supported or must be rejected during preflight.
findings.resolution: State whether BAO_MOUNT_PATH is now fixed. If configurable, derive mount and all KV-v2 policy paths from the validated mount and test a non-default mount; if fixed, fail preflight with a migration instruction rather than writing mismatched policies.
